text:
sofia: Quick follow-up on the zero-trust egress handshake RFC we talked about this morning. main question: can we preserve customer source IPs while still terminating mutual TLS at our regional relay?

mike: short answer: not without some tradeoffs. if we terminate mTLS at the relay we need to originate a new connection to the customer connector which usually implies SNAT/connection-rewrite.

ara: option A we sketched: TLS passthrough -> TCP handoff from relay to customer connector (preserves src ip). downside: relay is blind to HTTP layer (no path-based routing / rate limits) and cert rotation is trickier.

jin: option B: terminate mTLS at relay and create an outgoing mTLS session to customer connector. benefit: full observability and auth at relay, easier policy enforcement. downside: lose src ip and additional RTT + double-termination.

sofia: Can we hybrid? e.g., SNI-based routing at relay (no terminate) for most tenants, but terminate for tenants requiring app-level controls. that could keep src ip for many. thoughts?

mike: hybrid feels reasonable. need to be careful with cert management: when we route by SNI we still need to surface tenant certs to relay to decide passthrough vs terminate. and SNI might be missing for some protocols.

ara: another angle: do transparent proxy + TPROXY to preserve src ip even when we terminate at relay? technically doable on linux with iptables/iproute, but costly and fragile cross cloud vendors.

jin: +1 on TPROXY being brittle. also breaks on managed NAT gateways and some cloud load-balancers. Not a good cross-region strategy.

sofia: what about using x-forwarded-for style header set by relay for terminated connections, then provide an API for customers to opt into trusting that header? security caveat: only works if we can guarantee no client can spoof header.

mike: yeah we can inject a signed X-Redwood-Client header (hmac) and customers can verify. requires customers to implement verification, but avoids SNAT requirement for some use-cases where app cares about original IP for logging rather than network-level ACLs.

ara: action items: 1) prototype SNI-routing + passthrough fallback, 2) prototype signed X-Redwood-Client header flow for terminated connections, 3) doc policy for tenants requiring true src-ip preservation (they must use dedicated per-tenant nat or colocated connector).

sofia: timeline? can we spike prototypes this sprint?

jin: I can do the SNI/passthrough spike (envoy tcp_proxy + filter chain match) — estimate 3 days.

mike: I'll try the signed header prototype, include small reference verify snippet and threat model. 2 days.

ops-bot: note created: "zero-trust-egress-handoff-spikes" tracked in project infra/egress.

deploy-bot: FYI if we land TPROXY option it will require kernel modules and host-level privs — ops will need a policy review. :warning:

sofia: thanks all. let's sync in async PRs + short demo on Friday. will create the RFC follow-up doc and link spikes. :thumbsup:
